title: Integral compact supports have the prescribed reductions
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$. Fix $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Integral coefficients on a scheme $T$ mean modules over $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on the small pro-étale site, not over the discrete constant sheaf $R$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].

Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $d\geq0$ be an integer with $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-dimension]. Let $a\leq b$ be integers and $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Suppose that every derived reduction $K_n=K\otimes_R^L A_n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[a,b]$, in the intrinsic sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For the integral and finite-level compact-support functors defined in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], one has

$$
Rf_!K\in D^b_c(Y,R),\qquad
(Rf_!K)\otimes_R^L A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,n}K_n\quad(n\geq1).
$$

Every displayed reduction has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$. The displayed isomorphisms are the canonical compact-support coefficient comparisons, compatible with successive reductions.

proof.text: Write $B_{T,n}=(A_n)_T$ and $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n B_{T,n}$. By the definition of the integral category, each $K_n$ is intrinsically bounded constructible; by hypothesis its Tor interval is $[a,b]$. Choose a K-flat complex $P$ representing $K$, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat R_X}B_{X,n}$ represents $K_n$, and the maps $P_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}P_n$ are the termwise quotient maps for $m\geq n$. These are exactly the input reduction maps in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: input reductions; explicit K-flat model (Stacks Tags 06YS and 06YY).

proof.text: The comparisons $K_m\otimes^L_{B_{X,m}}B_{X,n}\to K_n$ are canonical isomorphisms with the quotient cocycle. Indeed $P_m$ is K-flat over $B_{X,m}$: for an acyclic $B_{X,m}$-complex $N$, its underlying $\widehat R_X$-complex is acyclic, and $P_m\otimes_{B_{X,m}}N=P\otimes_{\widehat R_X}N$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Thus [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes the comparison by $(P\otimes B_{X,m})\otimes_{B_{X,m}}B_{X,n}\to P\otimes B_{X,n}$. The tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives its inverse on pure tensors: $(x\otimes u)\otimes v\mapsto x\otimes\overline u v$ and $x\otimes v\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes v$. These balanced maps commute with differentials and sheafification. For $r\geq m\geq n$ both composites send $((x\otimes u)\otimes v)\otimes w$ to $x\otimes\overline u\overline v w$, proving the cocycle and compatibility with the actual quotient transitions.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: normalization of input reductions; balancing calculation underlying Stacks Tag 06YY.

proof.text: Keep fixed the compactification $c_0=(j_0,p_0)$ used to define all finite-level functors and their transition maps in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For the finite-level bound only, replace it by $c=\mathsf{Dense}(c_0)$. The open immersion $j_0$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target], applied to $X\to\overline X_0\to Y$ (the first composite is finite type and $p_0$ is proper, hence separated). By [def-nagata-dense-refinement] and [prop-nagata-dense-refinement], $c=(j,p)$ is a compactification of the same $f$ with ambient scheme $\overline X=\operatorname{SIm}(j_0)$. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], $j$ is also topologically dense. The ambient scheme is finite type over $k$: $p$ is proper, in particular finite type, and $Y$ is finite type over $k$ (finite generation of algebras composes on affine charts). Therefore [lem-kun-dimension-extension], for the dense open $X\hookrightarrow\overline X$, gives $\dim\overline X=\dim X\leq d$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: replace the ambient compactification by its scheme-theoretic closure and bound its dimension.

proof.text: For every $n$, apply [lem-trf-open-ctf] to $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ and $K_n$. It gives $j_!K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ with Tor interval $[a,b]$. Apply [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] to $p:\overline X\to Y$: both schemes are finite type over $k$, $p$ is proper and hence separated finite type, and $\dim\overline X\leq d$. It follows that $Rp_{*,n}j_!K_n$ is intrinsically bounded constructible with Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$. This pro-étale corollary packages the source's étale direct-image theorem and $2d$ vanishing bound, so no étale theorem is being applied directly to a pro-étale complex.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: extension by zero and finite-level direct-image Tor bound.

proof.text: To pass this bound back to the original compactification, first apply [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) to $K_n$. It supplies a bounded constructible étale-origin witness, exactly the domain required by [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]. That proposition supplies an isomorphism $Rp_{*,n}j_!K_n\cong Rf^{c_0}_{!,n}K_n$. Put $M_n=Rf^{c_0}_{!,n}K_n$ from now on. Isomorphic objects have the same constructibility and Tor interval: tensoring the isomorphism with any degree-zero $A_n$-module sheaf gives isomorphic cohomology. Thus every $M_n$ is bounded constructible with interval $[a,b+2d]$. We have used the dense compactification only to prove this bound, and all tower maps below use the one fixed $c_0$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: compactification comparison on its stated étale-origin domain.

proof.text:
For $m\geq n$ let $\tau_{m,n}:M_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}M_n$ be $Rf^{c_0}_{!,m}$ of the input quotient transition, followed by the restriction-of-scalars isomorphism of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. By that lemma's compatibility with composed ring maps and the quotient cocycle in Step 2, these maps have identity units and $\tau_{r,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{r,m}(\tau_{m,n})\tau_{r,m}$. Their adjoints under the tensor-restriction adjunction of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] are
$$
M_m\otimes^L_{B_{Y,m}}B_{Y,n}\longrightarrow Rf^{c_0}_{!,n}(K_m\otimes^L_{B_{X,m}}B_{X,n})\longrightarrow Rf^{c_0}_{!,n}K_n.
$$
The first arrow is the canonical tensor comparison of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change], and the second is $Rf^{c_0}_{!,n}$ of Step 2. To check that these are the adjoints of the actual transitions, use the adjunction formula $g\mapsto(x\mapsto g(x\otimes1))$: the tensor comparison, evaluated at $1$, is $Rf_{!,m}$ of the input unit map to the restriction of its tensor reduction, followed by the restriction-of-scalars comparison. This is precisely the displayed definition of $\tau_{m,n}$. The coefficient-change lemma explicitly identifies its map as this tensor comparison and asserts compatibility with its defining counits and successive reductions. Both arrows are isomorphisms: that lemma applies because $K_m$ is bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude, and Step 2 gives the second arrow. This verifies normalization for the specified transitions, rather than merely constructing unrelated reduction isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: coefficient comparisons normalize the actual fixed-compactification tower.

proof.text: The normalized-tower definition also requires a coherent derived realization. Here it can be supplied explicitly. Choose a complex $C_1$ of $B_{Y,1}$-modules representing $M_1$. Inductively suppose $C_n$ has been chosen with an identification $[C_n]\cong M_n$. In the derived category of $B_{Y,n+1}$-modules represent $M_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\tau_{n+1,n}}\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}[C_n]$ by a roof $V_{n+1}\xleftarrow{\sim}C_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}C_n$, using [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system]; here $V_{n+1}$ is any representative of $M_{n+1}$, and a representative chain map is chosen for the right leg in the homotopy category. The left quasi-isomorphism identifies $[C_{n+1}]$ with $M_{n+1}$. Restrict all $C_n$ to $\widehat R_Y$ and use the chosen adjacent chain maps; define longer transition maps by composition. The resulting strict inverse sequence of complexes is a complex of towers, hence an object of the derived tower category, whose evaluations and transitions are the required $\operatorname{Res}_nM_n$ and $\operatorname{Res}_m\tau_{m,n}$. Thus the coherent datum required by [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] exists. There are no additional relations to lift: the sequential index category is generated by adjacent arrows, and Step 6 identifies every composite with its prescribed transition.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: coherent realization needed to apply normalized-tower effectivity (Stacks Tag 05RT).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] to the tower of Steps 6–7. It says that $M=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nM_n$ is derived complete and that its canonical counit maps $M\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Y}B_{Y,n}\to M_n$ are coherent isomorphisms. This is the same inverse system, with the same adjacent maps, whose derived limit defines $Rf_!K$ in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]; use that defining limit for $M$. The effectivity comparisons are adjoint to its projections $M\to\operatorname{Res}_nM_n$. These are exactly the compact-support coefficient comparisons: Step 6 checked the specified finite-stage maps and their adjoints. The coherence asserted by effectivity gives compatibility with successive reductions. No boundedness is needed for this application of effectivity.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: effectivity gives the prescribed reductions and their canonical maps.

proof.text: By Steps 5 and 8 all reductions of $Rf_!K$ are bounded constructible with the common Tor interval $[a,b+2d]$. Taking the degree-zero module sheaf $B_{Y,n}$ itself as the test module in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] shows that the cohomology of every reduction vanishes outside $[a,b+2d]$: the unit identification $M_n\otimes^L_{B_{Y,n}}B_{Y,n}\cong M_n$ is given on a K-flat representative by $x\otimes u\mapsto ux$, with inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Thus the reductions have a single cohomological support interval independent of $n$. Together with the derived completeness from Step 8, these are exactly the membership conditions of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Hence $Rf_!K\in D^b_c(Y,R)$, and [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] gives the asserted uniform reduction Tor interval. This proves every clause without using the separate integral-constructibility theorem mentioned in the definition of $Rf_!$.
